This is not a Voat goat, but I thought I'd share another logo design from a failed start up company.

I was approached by the Greez Monkey Founder & Developement Team to create their primary logo branding. The company was intended to aggregate the data from all Tire and Automotive Service Centers and post the best deals (similar to a Hotels.com or Travelocity style service). The start-up costs and effort it took to codify all automotive service repairs ended up being too challenging for the client, and the site/business was scrapped during its Alpha phase.

The customer wanted an iconic mascot for their company, and stated numerous famous animal characters with brands (Firefox, Sonic the Hedgehog, & etc.). I drafted up 12 different monkey designs, and this one was the final cut. The circle in the back is a simplified tire. The customer REALLY wanted an actual tire with treads + sidewalls, but as with any logo design, we had to slim down the amount of detail (to make reproduction of the logo easier for all facets (apparel uniform embroidery, small screen printed promotional items, & etc.). The color scheme for the company was Black and Red.

Last note about the typography: I usually HATE, HATE, HATE, using gradients in a logo. But, for this automotive centric company the textured font worked. The "Z" was accentuated to help end-users understand how to better pronounce the company's name "Gree - Z" Monkey. I was never a huge fan company name, but apparently there are/were numerous Grease Monkey companies in existence, and rarely do I ever challenge a client on their company name.

Are we talking consciousness in general or are we talking reflexivity and self consciousness?

I agree that consciousness is that something "other" than patterns or body. It's the something that goes away when you die that you can see in the eyes.

To me it means self-awareness to the point of understanding one's own interactions with other beings and the environment, and the ability to change it accordingly. The vast majority of animals do not seem to possess this ability. They are living moment to moment and making instinctual decisions based on what's happening right now. They do not have the ability to comprehend the long-term and its results based on decisions made in the moment.

Good question. My pathetic attempt to answer would be that consciousness is the continual analysis of sensory input against an individual's short term and long term memory. Another way to put it would that it is the collective comparison of many slices of time (memories) as well as your immediate experience. It's the discrepancies between these slices of time that comprise your representation of yourself. This eventual representation of yourself is then reincorporated back into your collective slices of time, creating a feedback loop.
